definition: Transfer-based machine translation is a type of machine translation (MT).
details: It is currently one of the most widely used methods of machine translation. In contrast to the simpler direct model of MT, transfer MT breaks translation into three steps: analysis of the source language text to determine its grammatical structure, transfer of the resulting structure to a structure suitable for generating text in the target language, and finally generation of this text. Transfer-based MT systems are thus capable of using knowledge of the source and target languages.

explainer.lead: Transfer-based machine translation breaks translation into analysis, transfer and generation, using knowledge of both source and target languages. It is currently one of the most widely used machine translation methods.

tiers.eli5: First you parse the sentence's grammar, then convert that structure into the other language's structure, then write out the sentence.
tiers.practitioner: Systems analyze the source text into a grammatical structure, transfer it into a target-suitable structure, then generate target text. The pitfall is that errors in the transfer step propagate into generation.
tiers.paperLevel: Three steps: analysis of source text to determine grammatical structure; transfer of that structure to one suitable for target generation; generation of target text. Unlike the simpler direct model, it can use knowledge of both languages.

explainer.example: An English sentence is parsed into its grammatical structure, that structure is transferred into a French-suitable form, and French text is generated from it.
